subject: Chemistry
source_note: TIE (2023), Chemistry Syllabus for Ordinary Secondary Education Form I-IV

topics.title: Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry

sub_topics.title: Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
competences: (a) Describe the modern concept of atomic structure (Dalton’s atomic structure and sub-atomic particles)
(b) Describe the concept of electronic arrangements
(c) Use the concept of atomic structure to determine the atomic and mass numbers of an element
(d) Explain the concept of chemical formulae and nomenclature (valence, oxidation state, radicals and naming of binary inorganic compounds using the IUPAC system)
(e) Determine empirical and molecular formulae of common compounds
(f) Describe the concept of chemical bonding (covalent and electrovalent bonding)
(g) Describe the concept of chemical reactions (chemical equations, balancing chemical equations, and types of chemical reactions)
(h) Relate the types of chemical reactions with common processes in daily life such as burning of fuel and digestion in living organisms
(i) Describe acids, bases and salts (reactions of acids and bases with various substances) and their applications in daily life

objectives.text: (a) Describe the modern concept of atomic structure (Dalton’s atomic structure and sub-atomic particles)
objectives.resources: Diagrams, pictures, wall charts, simulations and videos illustrating Dalton’s atomic structure and sub-atomic particles
objectives.assessment_criteria: The modern concept of atomic structure is clearly described

objectives.text: (b) Describe the concept of electronic arrangements
objectives.resources: Diagrams, pictures, wall charts, simulations and videos illustrating energy shell diagram, and locally available materials for designing electronic models
objectives.assessment_criteria: The concept of electronic arrangements in atoms is clearly described

objectives.text: (c) Use the concept of atomic structure to determine the atomic and mass numbers of an element
objectives.resources: Models, charts and pictures showing the atomic number of elements, and wall charts showing the number of protons and neutrons of elements
objectives.assessment_criteria: Atomic numbers and mass numbers of elements are correctly determined

objectives.text: (d) Explain the concept of chemical formulae and nomenclature (valence, oxidation state, radicals and naming of binary inorganic compounds using the IUPAC system)
objectives.teaching_methods: Inquiry-based learning, Group discussion, Gallery work
objectives.resources: Valence cards, modern periodic table, wall charts showing oxidation states and common radicals, and labelled bottles containing different laboratory chemicals
objectives.assessment_criteria: The concept of chemical formulae and nomenclature are clearly explained

objectives.text: (e) Determine empirical and molecular formulae of common compounds
objectives.resources: Model depicting empirical formulae and molecular formulae, wall charts showing molecular fomulae and modern periodic table
objectives.assessment_criteria: Empirical formulae and molecular formulae of different compounds are correctly determined

objectives.text: (f) Describe the concept of chemical bonding (covalent and electrovalent bonding)
objectives.resources: Selected organic and inorganic structures, Computers installed with Chemistry software
objectives.assessment_criteria: The concept of chemical bonding is clearly described

objectives.text: (g) Describe the concept of chemical reactions (chemical equations, balancing chemical equations, and types of chemical reactions)
objectives.resources: Kerosene, candles, KOH/NaOH, HCl, glycerine, selected apparatus and equipment
objectives.assessment_criteria: The concept of chemical reactions is clearly described

objectives.text: (h) Relate the types of chemical reactions with common processes in daily life such as burning of fuel and digestion in living organisms
objectives.resources: Laboratory note book, heat source and fuel such as charcoal
objectives.assessment_criteria: The types of chemical reactions are clearly related with common processes in daily life

objectives.text: (i) Describe acids, bases and salts (reactions of acids and bases with various substances) and their applications in daily life
objectives.teaching_methods: Inquiry-based learning, Group discussion, Field trips
objectives.resources: Citrus fruits, vinegar, sour milk, apples, wood ash, tooth paste, baking powder, mineral acids, hydroxides and indicators
objectives.assessment_criteria: The concepts of acids, bases and salts are clearly described

sub_topics.title: Demonstrate an understanding of the physical and chemical properties of elements on the basis of their arrangements in the periodic table
competences: (a) Explain the changes in the physical and chemical properties of elements across and down the periodic table
(b) Use the electronic configuration of an element to locate their positions in the periodic table

objectives.text: (a) Explain the changes in the physical and chemical properties of elements across and down the periodic table
objectives.resources: Diagrams, pictures, wall charts, simulations and videos illustrating changes in the physical and chemical properties of elements across and down the periodic table
objectives.assessment_criteria: Changes in properties of elements across and down the periodic table are correctly explained

objectives.text: (b) Use the electronic configuration of an element to locate their positions in the periodic table
objectives.resources: Wall charts of modern periodic table showing electronic configuration of some elements
objectives.assessment_criteria: The electronic configurations of elements are correctly used to locate the positions of elements in the periodic table

sub_topics.title: Conduct experiments in Chemistry
competences: (a) Prepare acid- base indicators using locally available materials
(b) Use the prepared indicators to test acidity and alkalinity of substances found in the locality

objectives.text: (a) Prepare acid- base indicators using locally available materials
objectives.resources: Coloured flowers, coloured leaves, mortar and pestle, pieces of clothes, heat source, tripod stand lemon juice, tomato juice, sour milk, vinegar, soft drinks and NaOH
objectives.assessment_criteria: Acid-base indicators are correctly prepared using locally available materials

objectives.text: (b) Use the prepared indicators to test acidity and alkalinity of substances found in the locality
objectives.resources: Locally prepared indicator, POP indicator, MO indicator, lemon juice, tomato juice, sour milk, vinegar and soft
objectives.assessment_criteria: Acidity and alkalinity of substances found in the locality are tested using the prepared indicators
